mainTopic: The minimum amount of eating שרצים (creeping creatures) that makes a person liable to מלקות: a כזית or a כעדשה?
overview: רב rules that a person gets מלקות for eating שרצים only once he eats a כזית, because the Torah uses the word 'eating' for them. The גמרא challenges him with a ברייתא, praised by רבי יוחנן, that ties eating שרצים to their טומאה, so eating should be measured by a כעדשה. The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is about dead שרצים, which carry טומאה, while רב is about live ones. אביי objects that רב was explaining a משנה that includes dead שרצים. רב יוסף replies that רב was stating a rule on his own. Next, the גמרא finds a contradiction in רבי יוחנן, who elsewhere says eating requires a כזית. רבא answers that the כעדשה applies only to the eight שרצים the Torah sets apart. רב אדא בר אהבה then challenges רבא: by that logic, animals should also be split into set-apart and not set-apart kinds.

steps.title: רב: Eating creeping creatures requires an olive-bulk for lashes
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: a person who eats שרצים gets מלקות only once he eats a כזית, because the Torah uses the word 'eating' for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: For eating creeping creatures, a person gets lashes for an olive-sized amount. Why? Because the Torah uses the word 'eating' about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ruling from רב about the minimum amount of שרצים a person must eat to get מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's reason is that the Torah describes the prohibition of שרצים with the word 'eating' (אכילה). Throughout the Torah, 'eating' is measured as a כזית, so the same measure applies here. This is the position the rest of the passage will test.

keyTerms.meaning: Creeping or swarming creatures, such as rodents and lizards, which are forbidden to eat
He receives מלקות (lashes) as a punishment
An olive-bulk, the standard Torah measure for 'eating'
What is the reason?
Eating; in the Torah this word normally means a כזית

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says that Rav says:
Eating creeping creatures: one is flogged for it with an olive-bulk.
What is the reason?
"Eating" is written regarding them.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:41 says the שרץ "shall not be eaten." In the Torah, "eating" normally means a כזית.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: מלקות for eating שרצים requires a כזית, since the Torah uses the term 'eating' for them.

steps.title: A ברייתא links eating creeping creatures to their טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא taught by רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא before רבי יוחנן. It notes that the פסוק about שרצים begins by talking about eating and ends by talking about טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא teach before רבי יוחנן: 'You shall separate between the pure animal and the impure, and between the impure bird and the pure; and you shall not make your souls detestable by animal, by bird, or by anything that swarms on the ground, which I have set apart for you as impure.' The verse opens with eating and ends with impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to challenge רב by quoting a ברייתא. This step sets up the challenge; the actual conclusion that clashes with רב comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads 'do not make your souls detestable' as a reference to eating, and 'set apart for you as impure' as a reference to טומאה. Because both appear in one פסוק, the ברייתא is getting ready to compare the two. That comparison is what will create the problem for רב.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall separate (between pure and impure)
Do not make detestable; understood here as a ban on eating
Opened with... and ended with
Ritual impurity

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתָנֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Chanina teach
before Rabbi Yochanan:
"You shall separate between the pure animal and the impure,
and between the impure bird and the pure;
and you shall not make your souls detestable
by animal, or by bird,
or by anything that swarms on the ground,
which I have set apart for you as impure":
The verse opens with eating,
phrases.notes: "Don't make your souls detestable" is being read as a ban on eating them.

phrases.english: and ends with impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתָנֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge against רב's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that eating שרצים requires a כזית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא connects eating שרצים to their טומאה in one פסוק, preparing to set the eating measure equal to the טומאה measure.

steps.title: Eating, like impurity, is a lentil-bulk, which contradicts רב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that eating שרצים, like their טומאה, is measured by a כעדשה. רבי יוחנן praised this teaching, and it contradicts רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as impurity is with a lentil-sized amount, so too eating is with a lentil-sized amount. רבי יוחנן praised him, and this is difficult for רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its comparison, and the גמרא states outright that it contradicts רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead שרץ makes things טמא even when it is only the size of a כעדשה. Since the פסוק ties eating to טומאה, the ברייתא says eating also needs only a כעדשה, which is much smaller than רב's כזית. רבי יוחנן's praise shows that this teaching is accepted, which makes the problem for רב stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: A lentil-bulk, the measure at which a dead שרץ gives off טומאה
Just as... so too; a formula for comparing two cases
And he praised him
It is a difficulty

phrases.english: Just as impurity is with a lentil-bulk,
so too eating is with a lentil-bulk.
And Rabbi Yochanan praised him,
and this is difficult for Rav!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's כזית measure for eating שרצים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא, endorsed by רבי יוחנן, sets the eating measure at a כעדשה, matching טומאה, while רב requires a כזית.

steps.title: Dead creatures versus live creatures
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there is no contradiction. The ברייתא's כעדשה applies to dead שרצים, while רב's כזית applies to live ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, when they are dead; there, when they are alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying the ברייתא and רב are talking about two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's comparison to טומאה only makes sense for a dead שרץ, because only a dead one gives off טומאה. So eating a dead שרץ makes a person liable at a כעדשה. A live שרץ carries no טומאה, so the comparison does not apply, and the normal 'eating' measure of a כזית stays in place, just as רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there; a formula for splitting two sources into different cases
When they are dead
When they are alive

steps.whatToRemember: Eating a dead שרץ makes a person liable at a כעדשה, because eating is tied to its טומאה. Eating a live שרץ requires a כזית, as רב said, because a live one has no טומאה.
steps.confusionAlert: The first 'כאן' refers to the ברייתא (dead, כעדשה) and the second 'כאן' refers to רב (alive, כזית). Don't mix them up.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
Here, when they are dead,
phrases.notes: This "here" is the ברייתא with its lentil-sized amount.

phrases.english: there, when they are alive.
phrases.notes: This one is רב's ruling of a כזית.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן – בְּמִיתָתָן, כָּאן – בְּחַיֵּיהֶן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): the two sources address different situations
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's כעדשה seemed to apply to all eating of שרצים, which would contradict רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כעדשה applies only to dead שרצים, which carry טומאה. Live שרצים require a כזית, as רב said.

steps.title: אביי: רב was explaining a משנה that includes dead creeping animals
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges the answer that רב's כזית is only about live שרצים, because רב was explaining a משנה that covers dead שרצים too.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But רב was talking about the משנה, and the משנה says 'all the creeping animals,' even dead ones. Doesn't that mean a case where there is a little of this one and a little of that one?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the answer from step 4. He argues that רב's כזית rule cannot be limited to live שרצים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 4 said רב's כזית is only for live שרצים. אביי says רב was commenting on a משנה that says 'all the שרצים' join together, which includes dead ones. So the משנה must be talking about a mix of a bit of a live one and a bit of a dead one, which means רב's כזית covers dead שרצים too.

keyTerms.meaning: He is referring to the משנה (literally, 'standing on our משנה')
When they are dead
A little of this and a little of that, meaning two pieces combining into one measure

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: He is speaking to רב יוסף, who defends the answer from the last step in the next step.

phrases.english: But Rav was referring to the mishna,
and the mishna teaches "all the creeping animals,"
phrases.notes: The משנה says all the שרצים join together to make up the measure for מלקות.

phrases.english: even when they are dead.
Is it not where there is a bit of this one
and a bit of that one?
phrases.notes: He means a bit of a live שרץ together with a bit of a dead one.

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רב's כזית applies only to live שרצים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב was explaining a משנה that includes dead שרצים, so his כזית must cover dead ones too.

steps.title: רב יוסף: רב was just stating a rule, not explaining that משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the link between רב and the משנה is only אביי's own inference. רב was simply stating a rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: That inference is yours. רב was just saying a teaching on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends the answer from step 4. He says רב was not commenting on that משנה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's challenge depended on reading רב as an explanation of the משנה. רב יוסף denies that. Once רב's words stand on their own, they can be about live שרצים only, so the answer from step 4 still works.

keyTerms.meaning: An inference, a conclusion drawn from wording
Just a teaching on its own, not tied to a specific source

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him:
That inference is yours.
Rav was merely saying a teaching on its own.

steps.whatToRemember: The answer stands: the ברייתא's כעדשה is for dead שרצים and רב's כזית is for live ones, because רב was not explaining the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the challenger's assumption about the context of רב's statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב was explaining the משנה about all שרצים joining together, including dead ones.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב stated an independent rule, not a comment on the משנה, so his כזית can be limited to live שרצים.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן praised the lentil-size teaching, yet said lashes need an olive-size
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a contradiction: רבי יוחנן praised the ברייתא that says כעדשה for eating, but elsewhere he says one is flogged only for a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן praised it. They raised an objection: Limbs have no minimum size. Even less than an olive-size of a נבלה and less than a lentil-size of a שרץ make things impure. And רבי יוחנן said: One is flogged for them only for an olive-size!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the line from step 3 that רבי יוחנן praised the כעדשה ברייתא. It now shows that רבי יוחנן seems to say the opposite somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה says whole limbs make things טמא at any size, even smaller than a כעדשה of a שרץ. On that, רבי יוחנן said that for eating, one is flogged only for a כזית. That clashes with his praise of a ברייתא that says eating a שרץ is measured by a כעדשה.

keyTerms.meaning: And he praised him
Whole limbs (with flesh, sinews and bone)
A minimum measure
An animal that died without proper שחיטה
They make things ritually impure
They receive lashes (מלקות)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two laws here. The משנה is about טומאה (impurity), which has no minimum for a whole limb. רבי יוחנן's comment is about eating, which needs a כזית for מלקות.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan praised him.
phrases.notes: This repeats the line from step 3, where רבי יוחנן praised רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא for the כעדשה ברייתא.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
The limbs have no minimum measure,
even less than an olive-bulk of a carcass
and less than a lentil-bulk of a creeping animal impart impurity.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
One is flogged for them only for an olive-bulk!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge based on the praise mentioned in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's praise of the ברייתא that says eating a שרץ is measured by a כעדשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן himself says one is flogged for eating only a כזית, which contradicts the כעדשה ברייתא he praised.

steps.title: רבא: The verse speaks about the specific creeping animals it lists
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the כעדשה measure applies to the specific שרצים that the פסוק sets apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The verse is speaking about the ones that are set apart.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא settles the contradiction in רבי יוחנן's words. He splits the cases by which kind of שרץ is being eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah lists eight specific שרצים, set apart from all other creeping creatures. רבא says the כעדשה measure that רבי יוחנן praised is for those eight. For other creeping creatures, one is flogged only for a כזית, so both statements of רבי יוחנן can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: Set apart, here the specific שרצים the Torah lists
The verse is speaking about

phrases.english: Rava said:
The verse is speaking about those that are set apart.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:29–30 lists eight שרצים. Those are the ones "set apart" from other creeping creatures.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by type of שרץ
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's two statements are about the same creatures and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כעדשה is for the eight listed שרצים; the כזית is for other creeping creatures.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: Then animals should also be split into set-apart and not set-apart
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה challenges רבא: if being 'set apart' changes the measure for שרצים, the same split should apply to a בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said to רבא: If so, for an animal too, let there be a difference between one that is set apart and one that is not set apart.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה attacks רבא's answer. He says רבא's logic would force a split for animals too, which we do not find.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא made the measure depend on whether a creature is 'set apart' by the Torah. רב אדא בר אהבה argues that animals also have a set-apart group, such as kosher animals compared with non-kosher ones. Yet we do not find a different measure for each group, so רבא's reasoning seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: If that is so (introduces a problem that follows from what was just said)
An animal
Let them make a distinction

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said to Rava:
If that is so,
with an animal as well,
let them distinguish between one that is set apart
phrases.notes: For animals, the 'set apart' kind would be the kosher animal, which the Torah separates from the non-kosher ones.

phrases.english: and one that is not set apart.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's split between set-apart שרצים and other creeping creatures
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If being 'set apart' changes the measure, animals should also have different measures for set-apart and not set-apart kinds, and they do not.
